newsitem.title: FRANCE: L'Aeropostale says 1996 cargo traffic up 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: L'Aeropostale says 1996 cargo traffic up 4 pct.

text.p: L'Aeropostale transported 110,000 tonnes of cargo traffic in 1996, an increase of four percent on 1995, provisional figures released by the French airline show.
1996 turnover totalled 1.055 billion francs, five percent up on 1995.
L'Aeropostale operates a fleet of 21 aircraft made up of 15 Boeing 737-300QC, two 737-200QCs, two 737-200Fs and two 727Fs.
L'Aeropostale's fleet carries freight by night between France's major cities for French post office, La Poste, Chronopost, TAT Express and the Air France group.
L'Aeropostale's also operates an air cargo route between Paris-Charles de Gaulle and Cologne on behalf of Global Delivery Express Worldwide (GDEW).
By day, L'Aeropostale's fleet is used to transport around 1.3 million passengers a year on behalf of Air France, Air Inter and Air Charter on scheduled and charter services.

L'Aeropostale is 50 percent-owned by La Poste (with 10 percent held by its express distribution subsidiary, Chronopost). The remainder is controlled by the Air France group. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
